# Prompt file format
Source: https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/prompt-format/

A test prompt is a Markdown file that describes one end-to-end test case in natural language.

## File identity {#file-identity}

| condition | result |
| --- | --- |
| The path is inside `testDir`, ends in `.test.md`, and has a nonempty name before the suffix. | The layout derives the plan, grounding, and case paths. |
| The path is outside `testDir`, has another suffix, or is the bare filename `.test.md`. | The command stops with `PROMPT_PATH_INVALID` (exit 2). |

The `details.reason` field of that error is `outside-test-dir`, `not-test-md`, or `no-name`. `--list` does no eligibility validation, so it never raises this error. See [Reports](/ambercast/reference/reports/#errors) for the error contract.

`testMatch` and `testIgnore` control which files discovery finds. The `.test.md` suffix is an exact requirement of the layout, not a general Markdown rule. For pattern details, see [Discovery patterns](/ambercast/reference/discovery-patterns/#selection).

## Normalization {#normalization}

ambercast normalizes a prompt before it extracts anything from it.

| operation | rule |
| --- | --- |
| leading BOM | Remove at most one leading U+FEFF. A second leading U+FEFF and any U+FEFF elsewhere stay. |
| line endings | Convert each CRLF and each lone CR to one LF. |
| everything else | Keep it as is. ambercast does not trim, collapse whitespace, reorder, or reword. |

## Secret references {#secret-references}

After you consent to a proposed secret name, `generate` writes a secret reference such as `{{secrets.name}}` into the `secretRef` fields of the plan. A prompt never contains one. ambercast rejects a prompt that has `{{secrets.` outside code spans and code blocks with `SECRET_SYNTAX_REJECTED`, as [Legacy secret syntax](#legacy-secret-syntax) explains.

| symbol | definition | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SECRET_REF_SOURCE` | `\{\{secrets\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+(?:\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*\}\}` | `secrets.` followed by one or more dot-separated segments of ASCII letters, digits, and underscores. |
| `SECRET_REF_PATTERN` | `SECRET_REF_SOURCE` anchored at both ends | A secret-bearing field accepts a reference only as its entire value. |

Surrounding text is not accepted. A valid reference must fill the whole field value.

## Legacy secret syntax {#legacy-secret-syntax}

Older prompts could contain a grant line such as this one:

```markdown
@ambercast-secret {{secrets.password}}
```

ambercast no longer accepts this syntax. Remove every such line, then follow [Migrate secret grants](/ambercast/how-to/upgrade/#migrate-secret-grants). The current consent and allowlist model is in [Secrets in plans](/ambercast/spec/secrets/).

## Terminal assertions and instruction coverage {#terminal-assertions-and-instruction-coverage}

Each terminal success assertion must be covered by its instruction. Arriving at a URL is not proof by itself. State a heading, message, or element that is visible at the destination.

> …I reach the dashboard and see the heading "Welcome back".

## Literal-secret rejection {#literal-secret-rejection}

Before persistence or report serialization, ambercast checks generated or provider-derived JSON against the literal-secret policy. A detected value is rejected with `SECRET_LITERAL_REJECTED`, and the literal is not kept in diagnostics.

The one exception is an item in the provider's `assumptions` list. When it matches secret detection, ambercast replaces it with a generic message and continues instead of failing with `SECRET_LITERAL_REJECTED`. The policy does not reject prompt prose for containing text that looks like a credential. The detector contract is in [Secrets in plans](/ambercast/spec/secrets/#literal-secret-rejection).

## See also {#see-also}

- [Discovery patterns](/ambercast/reference/discovery-patterns/#selection)
- [Environment variables](/ambercast/reference/environment-variables/#secrets)
- [Write effective prompts](/ambercast/how-to/write-effective-prompts/)
- [Manage secrets](/ambercast/how-to/manage-secrets/)
- [Secrets in plans](/ambercast/spec/secrets/)

---

# Discovery patterns
Source: https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/discovery-patterns/

ambercast matches `testMatch` and `testIgnore` patterns against paths relative to `testDir`. The pattern language has two wildcards, `*` and `**`.

## Pattern language {#pattern-language}

The grammar has only the wildcards below. Every other character is literal.

| syntax | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `*` | Zero or more characters other than `/`, within one path segment (`[^/]*`). |
| `**/` | Zero or more whole path segments, including none (`(?:.*/)?`). |
| `**` not followed by `/` | Zero or more characters of any kind, including `/` (`.*`). |
| every other character | Literal text. Character classes, braces, extglobs, and other glob syntax have no special meaning. |
| the whole pattern | Anchored at both ends. A match on a substring does not count. |

## Selection {#selection}

| stage | rule |
| --- | --- |
| include | A path must match at least one `testMatch` pattern. An empty `testMatch` selects nothing. |
| exclude | A path that matches any `testIgnore` pattern is excluded, even when it also matches `testMatch`. |
| path form | The matcher receives `/`-separated POSIX paths relative to `testDir`, never absolute paths. |
| order | Discovery skips anything that is not a file, removes duplicates, and sorts the paths lexically. |
| missing root | A missing `testDir` gives an empty selection. Any other read failure becomes `FsIoError`, reported as `FS_IO_ERROR`. |

The sorted order is the stable execution order that commands use.

To keep a prompt out of normal discovery and still run it, exclude it with `testIgnore` and pass its literal path. `--list` does no eligibility validation on any selection.

## Defaults {#defaults}

By default, ambercast includes `.test.md` prompts and excludes run directories and both companion file suffixes.

| key | default patterns |
| --- | --- |
| `testMatch` | `["**/*.test.md"]` |
| `testIgnore` | `["**/.runs/**", "**/*.ambercast.plan.json", "**/*.ambercast.grounding.json"]` |

## Worked examples {#worked-examples}

| pattern or configuration | candidate | result | reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `**/*.test.md` | `login.test.md` | match | `**/` can span zero segments. |
| `**/*.test.md` | `nested/checkout.test.md` | match | `**/` spans the parent segment. |
| `ui/*.test.md` | `ui/auth/login.test.md` | no match | `*` cannot cross `/`. |
| `login.test.md` | `login.test.md.bak` | no match | The whole path must match. |
| include `**/*.test.md`, ignore `**/.runs/**` | `nested/.runs/cached.test.md` | no match | `testIgnore` wins after inclusion. |
| `{login,nested}/*.test.md` | `login/login.test.md` | no match | Braces are literal, not alternation. |

## See also {#see-also}

- [Configuration](/ambercast/reference/configuration/#key-table)
- [File layout](/ambercast/reference/file-layout/#companions)
- [Select which tests run](/ambercast/how-to/select-tests/)

---

# Reports
Source: https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/reports/

Each command can emit one JSON report with run metadata, a summary, errors, and command-specific results.

## Envelope {#envelope}

All objects in the public report schemas are strict and reject unknown fields. The schema defines a `review` branch, but the CLI has no `review` command.

| field | type and contract |
| --- | --- |
| `schemaVersion` | literal `3.11` |
| `command` | `generate`, `run`, `check`, `heal`, or `review` |
| `startedAt` | UTC string shaped `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ` |
| `durationMs` | non-negative integer |
| `summary` | strict object with non-negative integers `total`, `passed`, `failed`, `errored`, `skipped` |
| `errors` | array of `ReportError` |
| `results` | command-specific result array |
| `reportPersistence` | `run` only: `persisted`, `failed`, or `not-attempted` |

## Result shapes {#result-shapes}

The `results` array depends on the command. The next sections list each branch, including the ones only the schema defines.

## Generate results {#generate-results}

Every `GenerateResult` branch is strict. The optional fields listed are the only extra fields a branch allows.

| status | required fields | optional fields | forbidden fields |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `generated` | `id`, `file`, `planFile`, `dryRun: false`, `ambiguities: JSON[]`, `secrets` | `durationMs`, `aiCalls`, `warnings` | — |
| `would-generate` | `id`, `file`, `planFile`, `dryRun: true`, `ambiguities: JSON[]`, `secrets` | `durationMs`, `aiCalls`, `warnings` | — |
| `skipped-fresh` (`dryRun: true`) | `id`, `file`, `planFile`, `dryRun: true`, `secrets` | `durationMs`, `aiCalls`, `warnings` | `ambiguities` |
| `skipped-fresh` (`dryRun: false`) | `id`, `file`, `planFile`, `dryRun: false` | `durationMs`, `aiCalls` | `ambiguities`, `secrets`, `warnings` |
| `listed` | `id`, `file`, `dryRun: false` | — | `planFile`, `ambiguities`, `durationMs`, `aiCalls` |
| `failed` | `id`, `file`, `dryRun: boolean` | `durationMs`, `aiCalls` | `planFile`, `ambiguities` |
| `skipped` | `id`, `file` | — | `planFile`, `dryRun`, `ambiguities`, `durationMs`, `aiCalls` |

The AI provider can list assumptions that the prompt does not state, in an optional string array named `assumptions`. On `generated` and `would-generate` results, `generate` adds each nonblank assumption to `warnings` as `{ kind: 'generator-assumption', message }`. Assumptions never stop `generate` or `heal`.

The human-readable output prints `warning: <message>`, indented by two spaces, right after the result line. If an assumption matches secret detection, ambercast replaces it with `An assumption was omitted because it looked like a secret.`.

ambercast does not store assumptions in the plan. A re-run on a fresh plan returns `skipped-fresh` with no assumption warnings. Pass `--force` to regenerate and see the assumptions again. Regeneration is non-deterministic.

On `generated` and `would-generate` results, `ambiguities` is always `[]`. A provider's `ambiguities` means only that a step's target cannot be assigned.

For a single target, ambercast retries a response with nonempty `ambiguities` as `AI_RESPONSE_INVALID`, and exits 3 when the retries run out. An unresolved assignment across several targets still produces `PROMPT_AMBIGUOUS` and exit 2.

A consumer that validates warning kinds as a closed union needs the report 3.11 schema.

## Run results {#run-results}

Every `RunResult` branch is strict.

| status | required fields | optional fields | forbidden fields |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `passed` / `failed` / `error` | `id`, `file`, `planFile`, `durationMs`, `steps`, `sessions`, `explanation` | `aiCalls` | — |
| `listed` | `id`, `file` | — | `planFile`, `durationMs`, `steps`, `explanation`, `aiCalls` |
| `skipped` | `id`, `file` | — | `planFile`, `durationMs`, `steps`, `explanation`, `aiCalls` |

## Check results {#check-results}

Every `CheckResult` branch is strict.

| status | required fields | optional fields | forbidden fields |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fresh`, `stale`, `orphaned-plan`, `orphaned-grounding`, `missing-plan`, `missing-grounding`, `stale-grounding`, `invalid-grounding`, `fresh-without-grounding` | `id`, `file`, `planFile`, `reason` | `groundingFile`, `artifactFile` | — |
| `invalid-artifact-name` | `id`, `file`, `artifactFile`, `reason` | — | `planFile`, `groundingFile` |
| `listed` | `id`, `file` | — | `planFile`, `reason`, `groundingFile`, `artifactFile` |
| `skipped` | `id`, `file` | — | `planFile`, `reason`, `groundingFile`, `artifactFile` |

## Heal results {#heal-results}

Every completed `HealResult` branch requires `id`, `file`, `planFile`, `status: completed`, `durationMs`, `steps`, `sessions`, and `explanation`. `aiCalls` is optional.

Only a `healed` row can carry the optional `warnings`, which holds `generator-assumption` items from the `assumptions` of the accepted Stage 3 candidate. Other heal results forbid `warnings`. Assumptions do not fail Stage 3.

| repairOutcome | allowed application | allowed stopReason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `healed` | `applied`, `preview-only`, `declined`, `not-applied-interrupted`, `apply-failed`, `partially-applied` | `settled`, `attempt-limit`, `deadline` |
| `partially-healed` | `applied`, `preview-only`, `declined`, `not-applied-interrupted`, `apply-failed`, `partially-applied` | `settled`, `attempt-limit`, `deadline` |
| `unresolved` | `no-artifact-change`, `not-eligible` | `settled`, `attempt-limit`, `deadline` |
| `no-changes-needed` | `no-artifact-change` | `settled` |
| `listed` | identity-only: `id`, `file`, `status` | forbidden: `application`, `stopReason`, `planFile`, `durationMs`, `steps`, `explanation` |
| `skipped` | identity-only: `id`, `file`, `status` | forbidden: `application`, `stopReason`, `planFile`, `durationMs`, `steps`, `explanation` |

When Stage 3 rejects a full-plan candidate because its set of logical secret names changes, the completed result has `stage3Rejection: { reason: "secret-set-changed", added: SecretName[], removed: SecretName[] }`. The rejection is hard. No artifact is committed, and you must regenerate with consent instead of silently reassigning the candidate.

Every completed branch can also carry `repairTrace`, an ordered diagnostic array of the case's Stage 1, Stage 2, and Stage 3 attempts. Each entry is strict, so fields from another stage or outcome are not allowed.

| stage | outcome | other fields |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `stage1` | `accepted`, `no-advance` | `stepId` |
| `stage1` | `not-eligible` | `stepId`, `reason`: one of `frontier-out-of-range`, `mode-none`, `trace-current`, `no-confirming-step`, `no-confirms` |
| `stage2` | `accepted` | `stepId` |
| `stage2` | `rejected` | `stepId`, `reason`: one of `provider-error`, `response-shape`, `id-mismatch`, `secret-name-invalid`, `coverage-invalid`, `obligation-mismatch`, `literal-secret`, `no-advance`, `intent-invalid` |
| `stage3` | `accepted` | — |
| `stage3` | `not-passing` | `firstFailureIndex` |
| `stage3` | `failed` | optional `code` |
| `stage3` | `secret-set-rejected` | — |

A phase that admission denies adds no `repairTrace` entry. It shows up only through the case's `stopReason: "attempt-limit"` or `"deadline"`. Interrupted work never reaches a completed result. It is reported as `skipped`, so it has no `repairTrace` entry and no `stopReason`.

## Result statuses {#result-statuses}

Step and review results share these branches.

| branch | required fields | optional fields |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `step` | `id`, `type: action/assert/capture/ai`, `target`, `status: passed/failed/error/skipped` | `variable` on capture only, `kind: assertion/environment`, `expected`, `actual`, `screenshot`, `screenshotOmitted: secret-detected`, `observed`, `binding` |
| `observed` | `note`: the fixed `OBSERVED_NOTE`, `accessibilitySnapshot` | — |
| `review sufficient / insufficient` | `id`, `file`, `planFile`, `concerns[]` | — |
| `review skipped` | `id`, `file`, `status: skipped` | — |

After local verification, an action or capture step can carry `binding: { provenance: "grounding" | "quoted-match" | "ai-proposed", confirmed: boolean, quoteWaitMs?: non-negative integer, aiProposalMs?: non-negative integer }`. For `grounding`, `confirmed` is always `true`, because the binding came from an entry confirmed in an earlier run. It does not mean the entry was written in this run. For `quoted-match` and `ai-proposed`, it holds the value at case end. The timing fields appear only when those stages ran. Earlier binding failures report a case error instead.

Every executed run result and every completed heal result has a `sessions` entry for each target in the plan. Each value is `{ surface: "web", executor: { kind: "playwright", browser: "chromium" }, state }`, where `state` is `not-opened`, `closed`, or `close-failed`. `not-opened` means the target's launch returned no session, including when execution stopped before its first step. A failed close leaves the case status unchanged.

## Review concerns {#review-concerns}

A review reports its findings as concerns on the plan.

| field | type |
| --- | --- |
| `stepId` | string |
| `concern` | string |
| `suggestion` | string |

## Errors {#errors}

A report error is a strict object scoped to the whole run or to one case. Every entry has `scope`, `kind`, `code`, and `message`. `hint` is optional for every code, and a case-scoped entry also has a non-whitespace `caseId`. `details` is optional and exists only for the fifteen codes below.

Where `attempts` appears, it is `Array<{ attempt: integer 1–5, code: ReportErrorCode }>`. A `SecretRef` has the syntax `{{secrets.<identifier>(.<identifier>)*}}`.

| code | optional `details` shape |
| --- | --- |
| `AGENTIC_STEP_FAILED` | `{ stepId: non-whitespace string, actions: non-negative integer, assertions: non-negative integer, passedAssertions: non-negative integer, failedAssertions: non-negative integer, targetRejections: non-negative integer, lastFailedAssertion?: { check: "text-visible" \| "element-visible" \| "text-equals" \| "url-matches" \| "element-count", expected: string } }` Case scope only. The counters describe completed tool calls. |
| `CASE_ABORTED` | `{ reason: "run-reference-invalid" \| "run-value-missing" \| "secret-fill-incomplete" \| "agentic-no-terminal-evidence" \| "agentic-coverage-inexact" \| "agentic-proof-invalid" \| "grounding-secret-contaminated" \| "grounding-snapshot-invalid", stepId: string }` Case scope only. `reason` has eight defined values. |
| `AI_RESPONSE_INVALID` | `{ issues: Array<{ code: instruction-coverage, element-intent, or confirms issue code \| "text-equals-self-quote" \| "invalid-json" \| "schema-mismatch" \| "secret-allowed-name-not-projected" \| "secret-conflicting-target-names", path: Array<string or non-negative integer>, stepId?: StepId }>, attempts?: ... }` The `confirms` issue codes are `confirms-unknown-step`, `confirms-not-earlier`, `confirms-not-action`, and `confirms-duplicate`. The last two non-`confirms` issue codes always carry `stepId`. |
| `SECRET_LITERAL_REJECTED` | `{ detector: credential-prefix-sk \| credential-prefix-ghp \| credential-prefix-aws-access-key \| high-entropy-token \| embedded-secret-reference, path: non-whitespace string, attempts?: ... }` |
| `SECRET_ENV_VAR_COLLISION` | `{ envVar: non-whitespace string, refs: SecretRef[] }` `refs` has at least two entries. |
| `SECRET_CONSENT_REQUIRED` | `{ reason: "consent-required" \| "declined" \| "not-interactive", secrets: Array<{ name: SecretName, stepId: StepId, envVar: non-whitespace string, reason: string }> }` The inner `reason` can be any string. |
| `SECRET_SYNTAX_REJECTED` | `{ occurrences: Array<{ line: positive integer, column: positive integer, kind: "grant-line" \| "reference" }> }` |
| `BROWSER_LAUNCH_FAILED` | `{ reason: "executable-missing" \| "launch-failed", engine: non-whitespace string }` |
| `EXECUTOR_UNSUPPORTED` | `{ target: non-whitespace string, executor: non-whitespace string, reason: "surface-mismatch" \| "capability-missing", missing: UiCapability[], surface?: { target: "web", executor: non-whitespace string } }` |
| `PROMPT_AMBIGUOUS` | `{ ambiguities: integer at least 1 }` Case scope only. |
| `AI_EXECUTOR_UNAVAILABLE` | `{ attempts?: ... }` |
| `UNEXPECTED_CRASH` | `{ cause: { name: "Error" \| "TypeError" \| "RangeError" \| "SyntaxError" \| "ReferenceError" \| "AbortError" \| "TimeoutError" } }` |
| `FS_IO_ERROR` | `{ partiallyWritten: Array<"plan" \| "grounding"> }` Case scope only. |
| `PROMPT_PATH_INVALID` | `{ path: non-whitespace string, reason: "outside-test-dir" \| "not-test-md" \| "no-name" }` |
| `GROUNDING_UNRESOLVED` | `{ stepId: string, reason: "missing" \| "recoverable-miss" \| "no-candidate" \| "ambiguous" \| "proposal-rejected" \| "candidate-changed" }` For an element step, `missing` means no grounding entry exists, and `recoverable-miss` means an existing entry does not match the current page. |

For `AI_RESPONSE_INVALID`, the issue `code` is any of these values:

| code | family |
| --- | --- |
| `citation-whitespace-only` | instruction coverage |
| `anchor-invalid` | instruction coverage |
| `citation-checksum-mismatch` | instruction coverage |
| `criterion-id-duplicate` | instruction coverage |
| `criterion-range-duplicate` | instruction coverage |
| `criterion-order-invalid` | instruction coverage |
| `source-span-invalid` | instruction coverage |
| `source-span-whitespace-only` | instruction coverage |
| `success-criterion-missing` | instruction coverage |
| `intent-id-duplicate` | instruction coverage |
| `intent-id-missing` | instruction coverage |
| `intent-id-unknown` | instruction coverage |
| `intent-id-action` | instruction coverage |
| `intent-assertion-unsupported` | instruction coverage |
| `terminal-url-matches-forbidden` | instruction coverage |
| `verification-coverage-id-missing` | instruction coverage |
| `verification-coverage-id-unknown` | instruction coverage |
| `verification-coverage-id-action` | instruction coverage |
| `verification-coverage-index-duplicate` | instruction coverage |
| `verification-coverage-index-invalid` | instruction coverage |
| `verification-assertion-repeated` | instruction coverage |
| `intent-span-invalid` | element intent |
| `intent-span-whitespace-only` | element intent |
| `intent-citation-mismatch` | element intent |
| `quote-span-invalid` | element intent |
| `quote-text-mismatch` | element intent |
| `quote-unpaired` | element intent |
| `quote-outside-intent` | element intent |
| `quote-whitespace-only` | element intent |
| `confirms-unknown-step` | confirms |
| `confirms-not-earlier` | confirms |
| `confirms-not-action` | confirms |
| `confirms-duplicate` | confirms |
| `invalid-json` | other |
| `schema-mismatch` | other |
| `secret-allowed-name-not-projected` | other |
| `secret-conflicting-target-names` | other |
| `text-equals-self-quote` | other |

On `generated` and `would-generate` results, `secrets` lists the candidate secret uses that ambercast resolved. A dry-run `skipped-fresh` result includes it too. The optional `warnings` records non-fatal policy warnings of five kinds: `secret-name-reused-across-targets`, `secret-target-changed`, `allowed-names-truncated`, `action-unconfirmed` (with `stepId`), and `generator-assumption`. These fields make consent-related output observable without exposing secret values. For the high-risk `"*"` setting, see [Secret consent](/ambercast/reference/configuration/#secret-consent).

## Report persistence {#persistence}

Only `run` persists a report. It writes `runsDir/runId/report.json` with `JSON.stringify` of the finalized envelope.

The `reportPersistence` property records the write outcome:

- `persisted` follows a successful write whose JSON on disk equals the returned envelope.
- `failed` follows a write failure with no partial content visible.
- `not-attempted` applies when no write is tried, including a command failure before an outcome.

Only the writer is pinned to the current schema version. The viewer reads any 3.x report leniently. The examples below show one envelope per command.

```json
{"schemaVersion":"3.11","command":"generate","startedAt":"2026-09-06T00:00:00Z","durationMs":120,"summary":{"total":1,"passed":1,"failed":0,"errored":0,"skipped":0},"results":[{"id":"checkout.test.md","file":"checkout.test.md","planFile":"checkout.ambercast.plan.json","status":"generated","dryRun":false,"ambiguities":[],"secrets":[{"name":"LOGIN_PASSWORD","stepId":"fill-password","envVar":"AMBERCAST_SECRET_LOGIN_PASSWORD","allowed":true,"selectionSource":"target-slug"}],"durationMs":120,"aiCalls":1}],"errors":[]}
```
```json
{"schemaVersion":"3.11","command":"run","startedAt":"2026-09-06T00:00:00Z","durationMs":0,"summary":{"total":0,"passed":0,"failed":0,"errored":0,"skipped":0},"results":[],"errors":[],"reportPersistence":"not-attempted"}
```
```json
{"schemaVersion":"3.11","command":"check","startedAt":"2026-09-06T00:00:00Z","durationMs":0,"summary":{"total":0,"passed":0,"failed":0,"errored":0,"skipped":0},"results":[],"errors":[]}
```
```json
{"schemaVersion":"3.11","command":"heal","startedAt":"2026-09-06T00:00:00Z","durationMs":0,"summary":{"total":0,"passed":0,"failed":0,"errored":0,"skipped":0},"results":[],"errors":[]}
```

This section keeps an older anchor alive. See [Report persistence](/ambercast/reference/reports/#persistence) for the content.

# Error codes
Source: https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/error-codes/

ambercast reports run-level and case-level failures with a fixed set of error codes. Use this page to look up what a code means and which exit code it produces.

## Code vocabulary {#code-vocabulary}

Usage errors and environment errors have separate vocabularies. `SECRET_GRANT_UNATTRIBUTABLE` is the legacy exception. It stays in the report-code schema only for compatibility with reports from an earlier version, and no current error kind or report branch produces it.

| code | kind | scope | exit | condition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CONFIG_INVALID | usage | run/case | 2 | invalid configuration |
| PROMPT_PATH_INVALID | usage | run only | 2 | selected prompt path ineligible |
| SECRET_UNRESOLVED | usage | run/case | 2 | unresolved secret |
| TARGET_UNRESOLVED | usage | run/case | 2 | target cannot resolve |
| EXECUTOR_UNSUPPORTED | usage | case | 2 | executor lacks a capability or surface the plan needs |
| PROMPT_AMBIGUOUS | usage | case | 2 | generated response has unresolved target ambiguities |
| MISSING_PLAN | usage | run/case | 4 | plan absent |
| STALE_PLAN | usage | run/case | 4 | stale plan |
| INTEGRITY_VIOLATION | usage | run/case | 4 | artifact integrity fails |
| GROUNDING_UNRESOLVED | usage | case | 4 | grounding miss in an ai step or element step without `--resolve`; four other reasons can occur even with `--resolve` |
| SECRET_LITERAL_REJECTED | usage | run/case | 2 | literal secret rejected |
| SECRET_GRANT_UNATTRIBUTABLE | legacy | not producible | — | retained in the report schema for backward compatibility with reports from an earlier tool version; not produced by current `generate`, `run`, `heal`, or `check` |
| SECRET_ENV_VAR_COLLISION | usage | case | 2 | secret environment variable collision |
| SECRET_CONSENT_REQUIRED | usage | case | 2 | secret consent required |
| SECRET_SYNTAX_REJECTED | usage | case | 2 | legacy secret syntax rejected |
| BROWSER_LAUNCH_FAILED | environment | run/case | 3 | browser launch fails |
| AI_EXECUTOR_UNAVAILABLE | environment | run/case | 3 | provider unavailable |
| AI_RESPONSE_INVALID | environment | run/case | 3 | provider response invalid |
| AGENTIC_STEP_FAILED | environment | case | 3 | AI-directed interaction declared failure |
| CASE_ABORTED | environment | case | 3 | case aborted mid-step for a caller-correctable or environmental reason |
| FS_IO_ERROR | environment | run/case | 3 | filesystem operation fails |
| UNEXPECTED_CRASH | environment | run/case | 3 | uncategorized crash |
| INTERRUPTED | environment | run only | 3 | batch cancellation |

### AI response issue codes {#ai-response-issue-codes}

When a generated `confirms` reference fails validation, these `AiResponseIssueCode` values can appear in `AI_RESPONSE_INVALID` retries and report issues. `confirms-unsorted` is internal and never appears in retry feedback.

| code | condition |
| --- | --- |
| `confirms-unknown-step` | referenced step ID is unknown |
| `confirms-not-earlier` | referenced step is the same or later step |
| `confirms-not-action` | referenced step is not an eligible action or capture |
| `confirms-duplicate` | referenced step ID is repeated |

## Details by code {#details}

Only the codes below carry `details`. See [Reports](/ambercast/reference/reports/#errors) for the full contract of each code.

| code | `details` content |
| --- | --- |
| `FS_IO_ERROR` | In case scope, may contain `details.partiallyWritten` with `plan` and/or `grounding`. |
| `AI_RESPONSE_INVALID` | Normalized issues and optional retry attempts. |
| `SECRET_LITERAL_REJECTED` | The detector, the path, and optional attempts. |
| `SECRET_ENV_VAR_COLLISION` | The colliding `envVar` and the list of colliding secret references. |
| `SECRET_CONSENT_REQUIRED` | The reason (`consent-required`, `declined`, or `not-interactive`) and the unresolved secrets, each with its name, step ID, environment variable, and reason. |
| `SECRET_SYNTAX_REJECTED` | Each rejected legacy-syntax occurrence: line, column, and whether it is a grant line or a reference. |
| `AI_EXECUTOR_UNAVAILABLE` | Optional attempts. |
| `BROWSER_LAUNCH_FAILED` | A closed remediation reason (`executable-missing` or `launch-failed`) and the resolved engine name. The fixed remediation hint is the report-level `hint` field, not part of `details`. |
| `AGENTIC_STEP_FAILED` | The step ID, the completed tool-call counters, and an optional last failed assertion. |
| `CASE_ABORTED` | The closed abort reason and the step ID. |
| `PROMPT_AMBIGUOUS` | The count of unresolved ambiguities. |
| `UNEXPECTED_CRASH` | An allowlisted cause name. |
| `EXECUTOR_UNSUPPORTED` | The target, the executor, the reason (`surface-mismatch` or `capability-missing`), the missing capabilities, and optionally the surface. |
| `PROMPT_PATH_INVALID` | The path and the reason (`outside-test-dir`, `not-test-md`, or `no-name`). |
| `GROUNDING_UNRESOLVED` | The step ID and the reason (`missing`, `recoverable-miss`, `no-candidate`, `ambiguous`, `proposal-rejected`, or `candidate-changed`). |

## See also {#see-also}

- [Reports](/ambercast/reference/reports/#errors)
- [Exit codes](/ambercast/reference/exit-codes/#exit-code-table)
- [Troubleshoot common failures](/ambercast/how-to/troubleshoot/)

# Exit codes
Source: https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/exit-codes/

CI and scripts read the exit code to tell how a run ended. ambercast uses six codes, 0 to 5, and each has a priority rank.

## Exit-code table {#exit-code-table}

| code | meaning | priority (lower wins) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | success or no candidate | 5 |
| 1 | command-domain negative result | 3 |
| 2 | usage or configuration error | 0 |
| 3 | environment error | 1 |
| 4 | untrustworthy plan or grounding artifact | 2 |
| 5 | empty selection | 4 |

For example, [`PROMPT_PATH_INVALID`](/ambercast/reference/error-codes/#code-vocabulary) is a usage error and exits with 2.

## Aggregation priority {#aggregation-priority}

When a command has several outcomes, the code with the lowest priority rank wins. The order is 2 > 3 > 4 > 1 > 5 > 0.

The result does not depend on iteration order. With no candidate, the code is 0.

## Priority compatibility anchor {#priority}

This section keeps an older anchor alive. See [Aggregation priority](/ambercast/reference/exit-codes/#aggregation-priority) for the content.

## See also {#see-also}

- [Error codes](/ambercast/reference/error-codes/#code-vocabulary)
- [Reports](/ambercast/reference/reports/#envelope)
- [Troubleshoot common failures](/ambercast/how-to/troubleshoot/)

# Environment variables
Source: https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/environment-variables/

ambercast reads environment variables for the configuration path, the AI provider, secret values, and CI detection. It filters the environment before it starts an AI-provider child process.

## Configuration and provider {#configuration}

| variable | when ambercast reads it | effect | precedence and edge cases |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AMBERCAST_CONFIG` | when it looks for a configuration file | Selects an explicit configuration path. | A command's `--config` value wins. This variable comes next, then ancestor discovery, then the defaults. An empty value counts as absent, and any other value is used as given. |
| `AMBERCAST_AI_PROVIDER` | when it resolves the AI provider | Replaces `ai.provider` from the configuration with `claude`, `codex`, or `auto`. | `--ai` wins. This variable comes next, then `ai.provider`, then the default `auto`. An empty value counts as absent. A nonempty value other than the three is invalid. |
| `AMBERCAST_SECRET_*` | when a `{{secrets.*}}` reference needs a value | Supplies the value of one secret reference. | Dots become underscores and each segment is uppercased, so `{{secrets.a.b}}` reads `AMBERCAST_SECRET_A_B`. A missing variable leaves the secret unresolved. An existing empty variable is a resolved value. |
| `CI` | when a command applies its CI policy | Turns on the CI policy. | The policy is active when the variable is defined, nonempty, and not exactly the lowercase `false`. Values such as `FALSE`, `0`, and whitespace keep it active. The check is case-sensitive and does not trim. |
| `AMBERCAST_DEBUG` | when the CLI crashes, when `run` reports progress, and when the MCP server handles a crashed job or heal apply | Prints diagnostics to stderr. | Unset, empty, exactly `0`, and exactly `false` leave it inactive. Any other value activates it. The check is case-sensitive and does not trim. |

The mapping from a secret reference to `AMBERCAST_SECRET_*` is not one-to-one. Do not use references such as `a.b` and `a_b` together.

### What AMBERCAST_DEBUG prints {#debug-output}

When `AMBERCAST_DEBUG` is active, ambercast prints these diagnostics to stderr:

- The cause message and stack of a CLI crash.
- The name, redacted message, and stack of a run's unclassified case exception.
- The cause message and stack of a crashed job or heal apply in the MCP server.
- When a child process diagnostic exists, `child process: exit <n>` or `child process: signal <name>`, then `child stderr:` followed by the body or `(empty)`.

These diagnostics can contain sensitive text derived from requests.

### Provider resolution {#provider-resolution}

Provider resolution applies `--ai` first. A value other than `auto` is returned without probing. For `auto`, ambercast probes `claude` first and then `codex`. Each probe has an 8,000 ms deadline.

## Secrets and CI {#secrets}

| withheld variable class | passed to an AI-provider child? | rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AMBERCAST_SECRET_*` | no | ambercast removes the namespace, ignoring case, before every child invocation. |
| `AMBERCAST_ENV_*` | no | ambercast removes the namespace by the same case-insensitive rule. |

## Provider child environment {#provider-child-environment}

| passed variable class | passed to an AI-provider child? | rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| keys that do not match `/^AMBERCAST_(SECRET\|ENV)_/i` | yes | The runner copies the environment, removes only the denied keys, and passes the result to the child. |

The filter is a deny-list, not an allow-list. It returns a shallow copy and leaves the parent environment unchanged. `AMBERCAST_CONFIG`, `AMBERCAST_AI_PROVIDER`, and `CI` pass through when set, together with ordinary runtime and provider variables. ambercast makes no promise about the names of provider authentication variables.

## See also {#see-also}

- [Configuration](/ambercast/reference/configuration/#file-selection)
- [ambercast generate](/ambercast/reference/cli/generate/#flags)
- [ambercast run](/ambercast/reference/cli/run/#flags)
- [ambercast heal](/ambercast/reference/cli/heal/#flags)
- [Prompt file format](/ambercast/reference/prompt-format/#normalization)

# File layout
Source: https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/file-layout/

Ambercast resolves every companion and run path from the test directory and the runs directory. This page lists each derived path, its writer and timing, and the commit policy Ambercast applies.

## Companions {#companions}

| Input path | Derived path | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<testDir>/<dirs>/<name>.test.md` | `<testDir>/<dirs>/<name>.ambercast.plan.json` | Replace only the terminal `.test.md`. Preserve other dots in `<name>`. |
| `<testDir>/<dirs>/<name>.test.md` | `<testDir>/<dirs>/<name>.ambercast.grounding.json` | Use the same adjacent terminal-suffix transform. |

Forward mappings accept only an in-`testDir` path ending exactly in `.test.md` with a nonempty name. Invalid caller input raises `RangeError`. Inverse mappings recognize only exact in-tree plan or grounding suffixes and otherwise return `undefined`.

## Run artifacts {#run-artifacts}

| Artifact | Exact path | Writer / timing | Commit policy |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Prompt | `<testDir>/<dirs>/<name>.test.md` | You write it. Ambercast reads it. | Ambercast applies no repository policy. The procedure is in [Manage artifacts in git](/ambercast/how-to/manage-artifacts-in-git/). |
| Plan companion | `<testDir>/<dirs>/<name>.ambercast.plan.json` | `generate` writes a newly generated Plan. `heal` may replace it only after an authorized settlement. | Ambercast treats it as a committed input. It performs no repository operation. |
| Grounding companion | `<testDir>/<dirs>/<name>.ambercast.grounding.json` | `generate` creates or repairs it. `run` may write changed Grounding under the write-back policy. `heal` may replace it after settlement. | `grounding.repositoryPolicy` is `committed` by default and may be `uncommitted`. Ambercast performs no repository operation. |
| Invocation directory | `<runsDir>/<runId>/` | `run` and `heal` use one invocation identity for case evidence. Run IDs are timestamp-plus-UUID safe segments. | Ambercast applies no repository policy to this directory. `ambercast init` appends `tests/ambercast/.runs/` to `.gitignore` for the default `runsDir`. The procedure is in [Manage artifacts in git](/ambercast/how-to/manage-artifacts-in-git/). |
| Case directory | `<runsDir>/<runId>/<test-relative-dir>/<name>/` | `run` provides this directory to evidence capture for the case. | Same as the invocation directory. |
| Run screenshot | `<runsDir>/<runId>/<test-relative-dir>/<name>/<stepId>.png` | `run` writes it for an eligible failed live-browser step. Secret detection may omit it. | Same as the invocation directory. |
| Heal attempt directory | `<runsDir>/<runId>/<test-relative-dir>/<name>/attempt-<n>/` | `heal` allocates a positive ordinal per attempt. It confines that attempt's evidence and overlay under this directory. | Same as the invocation directory. |
| Heal screenshot | `<runsDir>/<runId>/<test-relative-dir>/<name>/attempt-<n>/<stepId>.png` | The shared capture path writes eligible failed-step evidence into the attempt-scoped case directory. | Same as the invocation directory. |
| Run report | `<runsDir>/<runId>/report.json` | `run` writes the finalized batch envelope after execution. [`ambercast view`](/ambercast/reference/cli/view/) reads it. A failed atomic write changes `reportPersistence`. | Same as the invocation directory. |

A screenshot is best effort. A capture or storage failure also omits it.

`runsDir` is configured independently and defaults to `tests/ambercast/.runs`. Ambercast does not derive it from `testDir`.

A `runId` must match `^[A-Za-z0-9]+(-[A-Za-z0-9]+)*$`. The pattern prevents separators, dot segments, and empty IDs.

`report.json` is written by `run`. The other reporting commands return their envelope without writing it.

# JSON Schemas
Source: https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/json-schemas/

Ambercast publishes JSON Schema draft 2020-12 files that validate configuration files, plan documents, grounding caches, and reports. This page lists the published metadata, the generated files, and what the schemas cannot express.

## Publication metadata {#publication-metadata}

Four schemas describe the current contracts on `main`. A schema version newer than the latest release appears in [Compatibility](/ambercast/reference/compatibility/#compatibility-table) once it ships.

| artifact | public path and `$id` | version | `title` | `description` | scope | state |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| config | `https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/schemas/config.schema.json` | unversioned; config has no `schemaVersion` | `ambercast config schema` | `Validates the parsed contents of a present Ambercast configuration file.` | A present configuration document. | available |
| plan | `https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/schemas/plan.v5.schema.json` | 5 | `ambercast plan schema v5` | `Validates the complete generated plan document that is reviewed and committed beside its source test prompt.` | A completed current `PlanDocument`, including targets and steps. | available |
| grounding | `https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/schemas/grounding.v4.schema.json` | 4 | `ambercast grounding schema v4` | `Validates the committed grounding cache associated with one plan digest.` | A `GroundingDocument` with `planDigest` and step-keyed entries. | available |
| report | `https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/schemas/report.v3.schema.json` | 3 (`schemaVersion: "3.11"`) | `ambercast report schema v3.0` | `Zod schema for the complete versioned output of a reporting command.` | A structured report envelope and its command-specific results. | available |

Five frozen snapshots remain for consumers of retired contracts. The site publishes them from committed files, and the npm package does not export them.

| artifact | public path and `$id` | version | `title` | `description` | scope | state |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| plan (historical snapshot) | `https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/schemas/plan.v2.schema.json` | 2 | `ambercast plan schema v2` | `Validates the complete generated plan document that is reviewed and committed beside its source test prompt.` | A frozen Plan v2 snapshot retained for consumers of the retired contract. | available |
| plan (historical snapshot) | `https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/schemas/plan.v3.schema.json` | 3 | `ambercast plan schema v3` | `Validates the complete generated plan document that is reviewed and committed beside its source test prompt.` | A frozen Plan v3 snapshot retained for consumers of the retired contract. | available |
| plan (historical snapshot) | `https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/schemas/plan.v4.schema.json` | 4 | `ambercast plan schema v4` | `Validates the complete generated plan document that is reviewed and committed beside its source test prompt.` | A frozen Plan v4 snapshot retained for consumers of the retired contract. | available |
| grounding (historical snapshot) | `https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/schemas/grounding.v2.schema.json` | 2 | `ambercast grounding schema v2` | `Validates the committed grounding cache associated with one plan digest.` | A frozen Grounding v2 snapshot retained for consumers of the retired contract. | available |
| grounding (historical snapshot) | `https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/schemas/grounding.v3.schema.json` | 3 | `ambercast grounding schema v3` | `Validates the committed grounding cache associated with one plan digest.` | A frozen Grounding v3 snapshot retained for consumers of the retired contract. | available |

Each `$id` equals its public-path URL. The site serves the four current schemas as byte-identical copies of the files in `dist/schema/`. The npm package exports those four as `ambercast/schema/<name>.json`.

The site configuration sets `site` to the `https://kotarotsubaki.github.io` host with base `/ambercast`. The publication URLs above use that host.

## Generated artifacts {#generated-artifacts}

| generated file | validates | generated from | npm export |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `plan.schema.json` | A completed current `PlanDocument` with Plan `schemaVersion` 5, provenance source, targets, and steps. | Zod `PlanDocument` converted as JSON Schema 2020-12. | `ambercast/schema/plan.json` → `./dist/schema/plan.schema.json` |
| `grounding.schema.json` | A `GroundingDocument` with Grounding `schemaVersion` 4, `planDigest`, and step-keyed entries. | Zod `GroundingDocument` converted as JSON Schema 2020-12. | `ambercast/schema/grounding.json` → `./dist/schema/grounding.schema.json` |
| `config.schema.json` | A present configuration document whose `$schema` is required and whose declared settings are otherwise optional. | Zod `RawConfig` converted as JSON Schema 2020-12. | `ambercast/schema/config.json` → `./dist/schema/config.schema.json` |
| `report.schema.json` | A structured report envelope and its command-specific results with Report `schemaVersion` 3.11. | Zod `ReportEnvelope` converted as JSON Schema 2020-12. | `ambercast/schema/report.json` → `./dist/schema/report.schema.json` |

`npm run build` compiles the package and then runs `node dist/schema-gen.js`. That script creates the schema directory recursively and writes the four schema files above. It also writes manifest files under `dist/manifest/`.

The checked generated files declare JSON Schema draft 2020-12 through `$schema`. Each also declares the `$id` shown in the publication metadata.

## Structural boundary {#structural-boundary}

Plan, grounding, config, and report JSON Schemas are derived from Zod. They are not maintained as separate handwritten definitions.

Duplicate plan step IDs are a Zod-only semantic refinement. JSON Schema 2020-12 cannot express uniqueness of a projected field across array items.

Validating only the generated plan JSON Schema does not establish duplicate-step-ID uniqueness. [Conformance](/ambercast/spec/conformance/) documents the combined boundary.

## Report schema {#report-schema}

`report.schema.json` is generated alongside the other schemas and exported as `ambercast/schema/report.json` → `./dist/schema/report.schema.json`. It validates the structured report envelope and its command-specific results. That coverage includes Report `schemaVersion` 3.11, required step Target identity, and the session inventory on executed run and completed heal results.

- [Grounding document](/ambercast/spec/grounding-document/)
- [Configuration](/ambercast/reference/configuration/#key-table)
- [Conformance](/ambercast/spec/conformance/)
- [Reports](/ambercast/reference/reports/#envelope)

# Compatibility
Source: https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/compatibility/

Each release pins schema versions and an element fingerprint tag. The tables below show which pinned versions each release uses and which changes force regeneration.

## Compatibility table {#compatibility-table}

| package version | Plan `schemaVersion` | Grounding `schemaVersion` | element fingerprint tag | report `schemaVersion` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `0.1.0` | `2` | `1` | `a11y-neighborhood-v2` | `3.0` |
| `0.2.0` | `2` | `1` | `a11y-neighborhood-v2` | `3.0` |
| `0.5.0` | `3` | `1` | `a11y-neighborhood-v2` | `3.5` |
| `0.7.0` | `5` | `3` | `a11y-neighborhood-v2` | `3.8` |
| `0.8.0` | `5` | `3` | `a11y-neighborhood-v2` | `3.9` |
| `0.9.0` | `5` | `3` | `a11y-neighborhood-v2` | `3.10` |
| `0.10.0` | `5` | `4` | `a11y-neighborhood-v2` | `3.11` |

Rows list 0.1.0, 0.2.0, each release that changed the Plan or Grounding schema version, and every release from 0.8.0 on. Schema versions on `main` after the latest release appear in this table when they are released. See [JSON Schemas](/ambercast/reference/json-schemas/#publication-metadata) for the schemas currently published.

In version 0.2.0, the provider request contract changed without incrementing the Plan schema version. That change updated `producerBundleFingerprint` and altered every prompt's `inputsDigest`, making 0.1.0 plans stale (see [Changelog](/ambercast/reference/changelog/#release-020)).

Schema changes are never migrated in place. Each transition has its own rule:

- Plan v1 and v2: `generate` treats either as non-fresh and regenerates a current Plan. `check` reports it read-only as `stale`. `run` and `heal` reject it with `INTEGRITY_VIOLATION` (exit code 4).
- Plan v3: it replaces the v2 secret-grant provenance model with consent and `secrets.allow`.
- Plan v4: it is not migrated in place and receives the same non-fresh, `stale`, and `INTEGRITY_VIOLATION` treatment.
- Plan v5: it replaces v4 element references with source-backed intent and adds `confirms`.
- Grounding v3: it replaces v2 bare-fingerprint entries with locator, fingerprint, intentDigest, and provenance.

For step-by-step upgrade procedures, refer to [Upgrade between versions](/ambercast/how-to/upgrade/).

## Regeneration boundary {#regeneration-boundary}

| change | affected material | obligation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Normalized prompt, Plan schema version, generator-template fingerprint, producer-bundle fingerprint, or named target definitions | `inputsDigest` and Plan freshness | Regenerate the Plan. Replay-relevant Plan content separately governs the resulting Grounding binding. |
| Replay-relevant Plan content | `planDigest` recorded by Grounding | Regenerate or replace Grounding; `generatorMeta` alone does not enter `planDigest`. |
| Accepted element fingerprint algorithm or preimage | Existing element-grounding entries | In `run`, an unusable source is a cache miss when it is absent, invalid JSON, stale provenance, or fails strict parsing without a coverage claim. Once a current-provenance source makes a coverage claim, its structural or canonical failure is an integrity failure and does not fall back. In `check`, grounding inspection classifies JSON/schema failure and a claimed non-canonical source as `invalid` and a stale `planDigest` as `stale`; the public report status is derived per repository policy in [Freshness and digests](/ambercast/spec/freshness/#freshness-consequences). |
| Report schema version or field contract | Structured-output consumers and persisted run reports | Update consumers for the emitted report contract. The [Changelog](/ambercast/reference/changelog/) lists what each report version changed. |
| Plan, Grounding, config, or report Zod schema | Published npm schema artifacts | Run the package build so the four JSON Schemas are regenerated from their Zod sources. |

The `inputsDigest` hashes exactly five declared inputs through canonical JSON and SHA-256. They are the normalized prompt, the Plan schema version, the generator-template fingerprint, the producer-bundle fingerprint, and the named target definitions.

Grounding freshness is a direct equality check between its recorded `planDigest` and the digest computed for your candidate Plan.

## See also {#see-also}

- [Changelog](/ambercast/reference/changelog/#release-020)
- [Upgrade between versions](/ambercast/how-to/upgrade/)
- [ambercast check](/ambercast/reference/cli/check/#status-vocabulary)
- [Freshness and digests](/ambercast/spec/freshness/)
- [Freshness consequences](/ambercast/spec/freshness/#freshness-consequences)
- [Specification changelog](/ambercast/spec/changelog/)

# Changelog
Source: https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/changelog/

This page lists product behavior and public-contract entries only. It leaves out repository architecture scanners, agent hooks, worktree lifecycle, lint configuration, CI, tests, the documentation site, and project workflow.

Releases 0.3.0 and 0.3.1 have no section because they have no product entries. Release 0.4.0 has no section because it made existing Plans stale through three producer-bundle revisions. Those revisions are `generatorSecretPolicy` 2 → 3 → 4 and `instructionCoveragePolicy` 1 → 2, so Plans from earlier releases are regenerated with `ambercast generate`. The repository's `CHANGELOG.md` also lists the other entries of those releases.

## Release 0.9.0 {#release-090}

Release date: 2026-10-08. Report schema 3.10.

| Class | User-visible entry |
| --- | --- |
| BREAKING | Report schema 3.10 adds the case-scoped error codes `CASE_ABORTED` (with `reason` and `stepId`) and `PROMPT_AMBIGUOUS` (with `ambiguities`). A `generate` or `heal` failure caused by an ambiguous prompt exits 2 with `PROMPT_AMBIGUOUS` instead of exiting 3 with a run-scoped `UNEXPECTED_CRASH`. Run rows that used to end without an error code carry `CASE_ABORTED`, `AGENTIC_STEP_FAILED`, or a case-scoped `UNEXPECTED_CRASH`. `heal` reports Stage 3 and final-replay failures as case errors, so the summary counts those rows as errored, and exit codes are unchanged. `ambercast view` shows error hints and details. |
| Feature | Every failure path yields a coded, diagnosable report error. |

Version 0.9.0 has one declared breaking change.

## Release 0.8.0 {#release-080}

Release date: 2026-10-06. Report schema 3.9.

| Class | User-visible entry |
| --- | --- |
| Feature | Report schema 3.9 adds `AGENTIC_STEP_FAILED` to case-scoped environment errors. It also adds the confirmation issue codes `confirms-unknown-step`, `confirms-not-earlier`, `confirms-not-action`, and `confirms-duplicate` to `AiResponseIssueCode`. |
| Fix | `generate` checks provider step IDs for secret literals before building diagnostics. |
| Fix | `generate` drops `confirms` references on `navigate` steps and reports violations by code. |
| Fix | `run` always reports `confirmed: true` for a binding from a confirmed grounding entry. |
| Fix | The runner classifies agentic step failures and polls AI-directed asserts until the deadline. |

Version 0.8.0 declares no breaking change.

## Release 0.7.0 {#release-070}

Release date: 2026-10-02. Report schema 3.8.

| Class | User-visible entry |
| --- | --- |
| BREAKING | Plan v3 → v4 adds required step Target names and removes Plan browser selection. Regenerate v3 Plans. |
| BREAKING | Plan v4 → v5 adds source-backed `intent` and `confirms` and Target-scoped `locale`. Grounding v2 → v3 replaces bare fingerprints with locator, fingerprint, intent digest, and provenance. Regenerate v4 Plans and their Grounding. |
| BREAKING | Target configuration moves from `targets.<name>.browser` to `targets.<name>.executor`, and the loader rejects the old key. The report gains `EXECUTOR_UNSUPPORTED` and `sessions[name].executor`. |
| BREAKING | The UI executor kind vocabulary is unified. An element step's grounding miss without `--resolve` reports `GROUNDING_UNRESOLVED` with exit 4 instead of exit 3 without a code. |
| Feature | Report schema moves to 3.8. Version 3.7 adds step Target names and per-Target sessions, and 3.8 adds heal Stage 1 `binding` diagnostics. |
| Feature | `ambercast init` scaffolds the configuration, a sample prompt, `.gitignore`, and `AGENTS.md`. |
| Feature | `ambercast view` is a read-only local viewer for `.runs` reports. |
| Feature | `targets.<name>.locale` sets the locale of browser contexts. |
| Feature | A UI executor abstraction adds capability preflight. |
| Feature | Heal Stage 1 rebinds element intents through `confirms`. |
| Feature | Element intent, quote matching, and intent digest primitives are added. |
| Feature | Plan IR v4 carries a per-step Target and one session per Target. |
| Feature | The MCP stdio server is added. |
| Feature | The MCP job model adds `ambercast_job_status` and `ambercast_job_cancel`. |
| Feature | The MCP heal apply takes two steps, with token issuance and elicitation. |
| Feature | Runtime event fan-out serves MCP, and heal preparation has two phases. |
| Fix | `init` adds a browser to the scaffolded configuration, plans BOM-safely, and aborts before applying on failure. |
| Fix | The MCP server emits `AMBERCAST_DEBUG` diagnostics for failed jobs and heal apply crashes. |
| Fix | The MCP server waits for heal apply confirmation and in-flight tool responses during shutdown. |
| Fix | The MCP server writes a stderr line when a progress notification fails to send. |
| Fix | Reports keep generation issue details in `AI_RESPONSE_INVALID`. |
| Fix | `run` recovers agentic target-resolution failures with diagnostics. |
| Fix | `run` takes the final poll sample at the deadline for assertions and binding. |
| Fix | `view` reads run reports from every 3.x schema version leniently. |
| Fix | `view` rejects default-port and non-authority `Host` headers and escapes `runId` in attributes. |
| Fix | `view` keeps screenshots and long text from overflowing the step table. |
| Fix | `view` applies the design system's dark tokens, status badges in the step table, and zero-omitted totals. |

Version 0.7.0 has four declared breaking changes.

## Release 0.6.0 {#release-060}

Release date: 2026-09-18. Report schema 3.6.

| Class | User-visible entry |
| --- | --- |
| BREAKING | Agentic MCP tool calls that fail schema validation no longer latch `INTEGRITY_VIOLATION` on the first mismatch. Up to 3 consecutive rejections per case return a structured result with the remaining budget. The 4th ends the case with `AI_RESPONSE_INVALID` (kind `environment`, exit 3) instead of `INTEGRITY_VIOLATION` (kind `usage`, exit 4). This change does not move the report schema version. |
| Feature | Report schema 3.6 adds the optional `repairTrace` diagnostic to completed heal results, and dry-run and apply produce the same result. |
| Feature | `run` waits for element presence before resolution. |

Version 0.6.0 has one declared breaking change.

## Release 0.5.0 {#release-050}

Release date: 2026-09-15. Report schema 3.5.

| Class | User-visible entry |
| --- | --- |
| BREAKING | Plan v2 → v3 removes secret-grant provenance. Remove legacy grant lines, regenerate with `generate --force`, and approve the candidate secret names through the consent/`secrets.allow` model. Plan v2 is not migrated in place. Report schema 3.5 adds the secret-policy error codes `SECRET_ENV_VAR_COLLISION`, `SECRET_CONSENT_REQUIRED`, and `SECRET_SYNTAX_REJECTED`, the optional `GROUNDING_UNRESOLVED` details, and the optional `GenerateResult` `secrets` and `warnings` fields. When a Stage 3 candidate changes the secret-name set, `heal` returns the `secret-set-rejected` result with `stage3Rejection.reason` `secret-set-changed`, plus the `added` and `removed` names. The legacy `@ambercast-secret` grant line and `{{secrets.*}}` prompt syntax are rejected with exit 2. |
| BREAKING | Existing Plans become stale and are regenerated with `ambercast generate --force`. Instruction-coverage criteria carry `startAnchor`, `startColumn`, `endAnchor`, and `endColumn`, and the `instructionCoveragePolicy` revision moves from 2 to 3. |
| BREAKING | `generate` stops at a consent gate for every newly detected secret name. An interactive terminal asks `y / N / i`, and any other run exits 2 and lists the unallowed names. Consenting appends the names to `secrets.allow`. |
| BREAKING | `run` resolves grounding misses with AI only with `--resolve`. `--cache-only` is removed and exits 2. `GROUNDING_UNRESOLVED` maps to exit 4. |
| Feature | `run` gains an agentic executor over an in-process MCP server. |
| Feature | Instruction coverage matches by anchor IDs. |
| Feature | Heal Stages 2 and 3 run under the allowlist model with secret-set invariance. |
| Feature | Secret naming is deterministic, and the allowlist is verified. |
| Fix | `generate` retries a provider response rejected for an embedded secret reference. |
| Fix | `BROWSER_LAUNCH_FAILED` is classified with a hint and details (report schema 3.4). |

Version 0.5.0 has four declared breaking changes.
