# Plan lifecycle and freshness
Source: https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/explanation/plan-lifecycle/

`check` judges freshness first. It inspects grounding only for a `fresh` plan, so a `stale` plan gets no grounding status.

## What a plan is built from {#provenance-inputs}

`inputsDigest` is a SHA-256 hash that records what a plan was built from. It covers canonical JSON that holds these inputs:

- The normalized prompt
- The plan schema version
- The generator-template fingerprint
- The producer-bundle fingerprint (`producerBundleFingerprint`)
- The definitions of the targets the plan references, which are the names in the plan's `targets`, sorted by name

Changing a target the plan does not reference changes neither the digest nor freshness. `executor` is not hashed.

With an unchanged prompt, a change to the schema, the template, or the producer contract still makes the plan stale. The producer-bundle fingerprint is separate from the template fingerprint because a contract change alone can change what generation produces.

Related: [Freshness and digests](/ambercast/spec/freshness/#inputs-digest), [Configuration](/ambercast/reference/configuration/#targets), [Compatibility](/ambercast/reference/compatibility/)

## How `check` decides freshness {#fresh-plan-decision}

`check` recomputes `inputsDigest` from the current prompt and the targets the plan references. It compares the result with `plan.source.inputsDigest`. A match gives `fresh`, and a mismatch gives `stale`.

A matching digest is not enough. A plan is also `stale` in each of these cases:

- The JSON is invalid.
- Schema validation fails.
- The serialization is not canonical.
- Instruction coverage is invalid.
- An element intent or a source span is invalid.
- The plan uses a retired `schemaVersion` (4).
- A target the plan references is missing from the configuration.

This keeps a broken plan from being reported as `fresh`.

Related: [ambercast check](/ambercast/reference/cli/check/#results), [Recover stale artifacts](/ambercast/how-to/recover-stale-artifacts/#stale)

## How grounding binds to a plan {#grounding-binding}

A `fresh` plan can still be unreplayable, because replay also needs grounding.

`planDigest` hashes the replay-relevant content of a plan, without `generatorMeta`. Grounding is current only when its recorded `planDigest` equals the one computed from the plan. Plan freshness and the grounding binding are judged separately.

`check` reports `missing-grounding` when grounding is absent, `invalid-grounding` when it is invalid, and `stale-grounding` when it is bound to another plan. When the repository policy is `uncommitted`, a `fresh` plan without valid grounding is reported as `fresh-without-grounding`. That is not a freshness failure.

`check` also scans in the opposite direction. An artifact with no matching test is reported as `orphaned-plan` or `orphaned-grounding`. A name that cannot be traced back to a test is reported as `invalid-artifact-name`.

Related: [Grounding document](/ambercast/spec/grounding-document/#plan-digest), [Reports](/ambercast/reference/reports/#check-results)

## What freshness hands off {#freshness-handoff}

`check` makes no AI call, launches no browser, and writes nothing. Its freshness answer says only whether the plan matches today's inputs.

Problems that appear during replay are separate. When the UI changes and an element fingerprint no longer matches, the result is `fingerprint-mismatch`. That is drift, a runtime condition, and it does not change `inputsDigest`.

Replay or healing takes over from there.

Related: [Replay and grounding](/ambercast/explanation/replay-and-grounding/#drift-handoff), [Healing model](/ambercast/explanation/healing-model/#three-stages), [Operating contract](/ambercast/agents/operating-contract/#command-contract)

---

# Replay and grounding
Source: https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/explanation/replay-and-grounding/

Replay reuses what ambercast recorded. Where the record is missing or unusable, replay stops unless you opt in to live resolution.

## Grounding as replay evidence {#grounding-as-replay-evidence}

`run` consumes grounding for `ai` steps and for element-binding steps: click, press, fill, fill-secret, and capture. Navigation and every assertion check the live page directly, without a grounding lookup.

An element entry stores a locator, a fingerprint, an intent digest, and provenance. Resolution uses the stored locator and checks the fingerprint. The [grounding document](/ambercast/spec/grounding-document/) defines the entry shape.

The resolver tells a hit apart from `fingerprint-mismatch`, `element-not-found`, `ambiguous-match`, `snapshot-invalid`, and `secret-contaminated`. A mismatch is never treated as a hit. `snapshot-invalid` and `secret-contaminated` abort the case.

Replay then follows one of four paths:

- A valid entry replays with zero AI calls.
- An integrity failure fails closed, whether or not you pass `--resolve`.
- A recoverable miss with `--resolve` is resolved live.
- A recoverable miss without `--resolve` stops with `GROUNDING_UNRESOLVED` (exit 4).

Related: [Grounding document](/ambercast/spec/grounding-document/), [Element fingerprint](/ambercast/spec/fingerprint/), [ambercast run](/ambercast/reference/cli/run/#ai-calls)

## When grounding hits {#grounding-hit}

A covered, valid AI trace replays without resolving an AI executor. Replay takes this path before it considers any agentic fallback.

When an element resolves as a hit, replay passes the stored fingerprint along and requests no new resolution. A complete cache runs without probing a provider, and a hit emits no AI-call event.

Related: [ambercast run](/ambercast/reference/cli/run/#replay), [Determinism in CI](/ambercast/explanation/determinism-in-ci/#bounded-side-effects)

## A miss with explicit resolution {#miss-with-explicit-resolution}

Grounding that fails its integrity checks fails closed even with `--resolve`. Invalid JSON and a failed coverage or verification proof are examples.

`--resolve` applies to two cases: grounding that is absent, and entries that are structurally valid but recoverable. Grounding written by a retired format version is one of the recoverable cases. For a plan with element-binding steps, `run` reports it as `GROUNDING_UNRESOLVED` without `--resolve`, and `run --resolve --update-cache` regenerates it.

With `--resolve`, an element miss is resolved live. ambercast writes the entry only when every step that confirms the binding passes and the write-back gate allows it. The gate depends on `localWriteBack`, `--update-cache`, and `ci.updateGroundingCache`.

Related: [ambercast run](/ambercast/reference/cli/run/#grounding-write-back), [Control grounding write-back](/ambercast/how-to/control-grounding-writeback/)

## A miss without resolution {#unresolved-miss}

Without `--resolve`, `run` resolves neither a cold-start miss nor a recoverable miss live. During an AI-directed replay, an `ai` step with no usable trace fails closed as `grounding-unresolved` (exit 4) and points to `--resolve`.

An element miss fails closed in the same way, with exit 4, instead of resolving the element live.

Related: [ambercast run](/ambercast/reference/cli/run/#resolve), [Reading structured output](/ambercast/agents/reading-structured-output/#decision-tree)

## Handing drift over {#drift-handoff}

A `fingerprint-mismatch` means the current fingerprint of the matched element differs from the stored one. `run` records it as a classification of its own, distinct from a successful resolution.

Healing starts with a fail-closed baseline replay. It attempts a repair only when a failure remains.

Related: [Healing model](/ambercast/explanation/healing-model/#three-stages), [Healing a test after a UI change](/ambercast/tutorials/repair-your-first-drift/)

---

# Healing model
Source: https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/explanation/healing-model/

When you change your app's UI, a previously passing test can suddenly fail. A moved element or a changed button label is a typical cause.

ambercast's healing feature investigates the cause of a failure automatically and tries to repair the test. It never runs unbounded: each case has a time budget, and changes to the Plan and Grounding files are written only after your confirmation.

## Safe precondition {#safe-precondition}

Healing accesses your running app and tries different fixes to find one that works. If the app doesn't reset to the same state no matter how many times you access it, repeated attempts risk piling up data or corrupting the app's state.

ambercast therefore refuses to heal unless your config declares the target with `healReplayIsolation: "idempotent"` — safe to replay repeatedly. It stops before it opens a browser or calls an AI provider. Omit the declaration, and it defaults to the safer `stateful` value — state changes on each replay — where healing still refuses to run.

In CI, nobody watches the result as it happens, so healing doesn't run unless you enable the `ci.heal` setting. The mode that only lists what it could fix makes no real change to your app, so it runs without that restriction.

Related: [ambercast heal](/ambercast/reference/cli/heal/#preconditions), [Configuration](/ambercast/reference/configuration/#targets), [Determinism in CI](/ambercast/explanation/determinism-in-ci/#heal-refusal)

## Three-stage escalation {#three-stages}

Healing first replays the test the normal way, without calling an AI provider, to confirm the failure actually reproduces. If it doesn't reproduce, healing stops there and makes no repair.

When the failure reproduces, healing re-measures with resolution enabled. If every step then passes, healing ends without a repair. Only a remaining failure, when a repair can start, moves on to the three stages below.

<figure class="ac-flow" aria-label="heal's three-stage escalation. The baseline replay ends healing without a repair when nothing fails. On a failure, re-measure with resolution enabled; go on only if a failure remains and a repair can start. If every step then passes, healing ends without a repair. Stage 1 fixes the grounding at the first failed point. If the failed point doesn't advance, stage 2 fixes one step or the tail. If a failure remains before the deadline, stage 3 rebuilds the whole plan; past the deadline, healing starts no new repair. Plan and Grounding writes happen only after confirmation.">
<div class="ac-flow-node"><div class="ac-flow-head"><span class="ac-flow-num">BASELINE</span><span class="ac-flow-chip ac-flow-chip-replay">No AI calls</span></div><p class="ac-flow-title">Replay the baseline fail-closed</p><p class="ac-flow-note">No failure means healing ends without a repair</p></div>
<div class="ac-flow-link"><svg aria-hidden="true" viewbox="0 0 28 52" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M14 2v46M8 42l6 6 6-6"></path></svg><span class="ac-flow-cond"><b>On a failure</b>, re-measure with resolution enabled; go on only if a failure remains and a repair can start</span></div>
<div class="ac-flow-node ac-flow-stage"><div class="ac-flow-head"><span class="ac-flow-num">STAGE 1</span><span class="ac-flow-chip ac-flow-chip-ai">May call AI</span></div><p class="ac-flow-title">Fix the grounding</p><div class="ac-flow-meter ac-flow-meter-s"><div class="ac-flow-track"><div class="ac-flow-fill"></div></div><span>the first failed point</span></div><p class="ac-flow-body">Healing re-locates the element at the failed point. If the point advances, it logs the fix as either re-grounding the element or an AI re-trace.</p></div>
<div class="ac-flow-link ac-flow-link-stage"><svg aria-hidden="true" viewbox="0 0 28 52" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M14 2v46M8 42l6 6 6-6"></path></svg><span class="ac-flow-cond"><b>If the failed point doesn't advance</b></span></div>
<div class="ac-flow-node ac-flow-stage"><div class="ac-flow-head"><span class="ac-flow-num">STAGE 2</span><span class="ac-flow-chip ac-flow-chip-ai">May call AI</span></div><p class="ac-flow-title">Fix one step or the rest</p><div class="ac-flow-meter ac-flow-meter-m"><div class="ac-flow-track"><div class="ac-flow-fill"></div></div><span>a single step or the tail</span></div><p class="ac-flow-body">Healing fixes the one failed step, or that step and every step after it together.</p></div>
<div class="ac-flow-link ac-flow-link-stage"><svg aria-hidden="true" viewbox="0 0 28 52" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M14 2v46M8 42l6 6 6-6"></path></svg><span class="ac-flow-cond"><b>If a failure remains before the deadline</b></span></div>
<div class="ac-flow-node ac-flow-stage"><div class="ac-flow-head"><span class="ac-flow-num">STAGE 3</span><span class="ac-flow-chip ac-flow-chip-ai">May call AI</span></div><p class="ac-flow-title">Rebuild the whole plan</p><div class="ac-flow-meter ac-flow-meter-l"><div class="ac-flow-track"><div class="ac-flow-fill"></div></div><span>the whole plan</span></div><p class="ac-flow-body">Healing resolves an AI executor, calls generate, and rebuilds the whole plan.</p></div>
</figure>

Healing tries the lightest fix first and escalates only when needed, to avoid unnecessary AI calls and cost.

Related: [ambercast heal](/ambercast/reference/cli/heal/#repair-model), [Steps](/ambercast/spec/steps/), [Replay and grounding](/ambercast/explanation/replay-and-grounding/#drift-handoff)

## Budgets that limit repair count and time {#repair-budgets}

You can set two kinds of limits so healing doesn't keep trying forever.

- `heal.maxStepRepairs`: the limit on AI dispatches during stage 1 and stage 2 repair, charged at dispatch time. Stage 3 still calls AI but doesn't count against this limit. Set it as a positive integer; omit it and there is no limit.
- `heal.caseTimeoutMs`: the time limit, in milliseconds, for healing one case. ambercast fixes each case's deadline before that case's first replay starts. When you select several tests, the whole command can take longer than this value. Past the deadline, it starts no new repair, but it doesn't force-stop work already in progress or discard a repair already produced.

Related: [Configuration](/ambercast/reference/configuration/#heal), [ambercast heal](/ambercast/reference/cli/heal/#limits)

## Plan and Grounding writes wait for confirmation {#confirmation-and-writes}

Finding a repair doesn't change the Plan or Grounding file yet. Healing holds each candidate repair in a temporary location and writes it to the real file only after you answer the CLI's confirmation prompt, or after `--yes` answers it in advance. Review the proposed change before you confirm.

This lets you see exactly which file changes, and how, before the write happens.

:::caution
Passing `--dry-run` skips the confirmation prompt and never commits a Plan or Grounding change, but a replay attempt can still write evidence under the runs directory. `--yes` pre-authorizes the CLI's confirmation prompt only; it isn't your own review and approval of the change.

When an agent runs ambercast without `--yes` and without a way to confirm interactively, ambercast stops with an error instead of writing silently.

:::

Related: [ambercast heal](/ambercast/reference/cli/heal/#confirmation), [Operating contract](/ambercast/agents/operating-contract/#command-contract), [Review generated diffs](/ambercast/how-to/review-generated-diffs/)

---

# Trust and security
Source: https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/explanation/trust-and-security/

ambercast checks each input at a boundary before it uses it, and anything that fails the check stops there.

## Artifacts and provider output are validated {#artifact-and-provider-boundaries}

`run` uses a plan only after it passes plan validation, including instruction coverage.

Steps that a provider generates are not saved as they arrive. ambercast parses them against the local response contract and checks instruction coverage. It saves them only after they parse as a complete plan.

For secrets, proposing and authorizing are separate. The provider can only propose a secret name. ambercast resolves every committed secret reference locally. It saves a candidate only when the name is on the allowlist or you give consent interactively.

`secrets.allow: "*"` skips the per-name review. It is a deliberate high-risk setting, never an implicit default.

Related: [Plan document](/ambercast/spec/plan-document/), [Conformance](/ambercast/spec/conformance/), [Error codes](/ambercast/reference/error-codes/)

## Page content is not an instruction {#untrusted-page-data}

ambercast treats content from the application under test as data, not as an instruction to an agent. When it captures accessibility evidence from a page, the evidence carries a fixed notice that page content is not an instruction. The notice is a mitigation, not an isolation boundary, so page content stays a risk to review.

The report schema is the public source of truth for `errors[].code`. Implementation-specific error classes stay out of the public contract.

Related: [Reports](/ambercast/reference/reports/), [Error codes](/ambercast/reference/error-codes/), [Reading structured output](/ambercast/agents/reading-structured-output/)

## Page evidence is redacted before reuse {#page-evidence-boundary}

ambercast redacts resolved secret values from accessibility-tree strings and keys before it sends or saves that data. It does not redact screenshot pixels. Snapshots sent to the AI exclude screenshot bytes.

Evidence for a step that fails during a live run uses redacted accessibility data. When it is uncertain whether a secret is present, ambercast skips the screenshot.

Redaction covers the resolved secrets and run-state values that replay knows. It does not remove arbitrary personal data that comes from the page. That data can remain in `actual` text, snapshots, screenshots, canvas, images, and CSS-rendered pixels. A gap between the scan and the screenshot can also leave data behind. Treat persisted reports and evidence as sensitive, and limit who can access them and how long you keep them.

Related: [Secrets in plans](/ambercast/spec/secrets/), [Reports](/ambercast/reference/reports/)

## Secret sinks are checked before a fill {#secret-sink-boundary}

Browser writes do not rely on the process environment as a boundary. ambercast checks the sink origin of each entry. A `fill-secret` trace action performs that check before it resolves the secret and binds the browser.

Related: [Manage secrets](/ambercast/how-to/manage-secrets/), [Configuration](/ambercast/reference/configuration/)

## Secret namespaces stay out of provider processes {#secret-boundary}

Configured AI providers run without access to the secret namespaces that ambercast manages. A provider child process receives a copy of the environment without `AMBERCAST_SECRET_*` and `AMBERCAST_ENV_*`. The match is case-insensitive.

Secret validation, generator policy, and report redaction each have their own role. A schema alone cannot prove that a value stayed secret.

Secret values resolve only at runtime, from `AMBERCAST_SECRET_<NAME>`. Providers see names, never values. A descriptive name is still not harmless, so review each proposed name before you approve it.

Related: [Manage secrets](/ambercast/how-to/manage-secrets/), [Environment variables](/ambercast/reference/environment-variables/), [Security policy](/ambercast/reference/security-policy/)

---

# Determinism in CI
Source: https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/explanation/determinism-in-ci/

These rules keep a CI run predictable: inspection cannot change anything, and the exit code does not depend on iteration order.

## Read-only inspection {#read-only-check}

`check` has no access to an AI executor, a browser, secrets, a clock, or events. Its storage access is read-only. Read-only is therefore structural, not a convention.

Reads and existence checks are enough to inspect prompts, plans, grounding, and orphaned artifacts.

Related: [ambercast check](/ambercast/reference/cli/check/#read-only-contract), [Plan lifecycle and freshness](/ambercast/explanation/plan-lifecycle/#fresh-plan-decision)

## Replay writes are bounded {#bounded-side-effects}

`run` writes its report JSON only to the report path of that invocation. It finalizes the envelope as `persisted` before the write. After a successful write, the file equals the returned envelope.

If the write fails, `run` returns the envelope with `reportPersistence: "failed"`. In that case only an otherwise-0 exit becomes 3. Exits 1, 2, 4, and 5 normally stay as they are. `not-attempted` means no write was tried, and `failed` means no partial content became visible.

In CI, writing grounding back needs `--update-cache` or `ci.updateGroundingCache: true`. The [configuration reference](/ambercast/reference/configuration/#grounding) covers the details.

Related: [Reports](/ambercast/reference/reports/#persistence), [ambercast run](/ambercast/reference/cli/run/#grounding-write-back)

## Healing is refused by default in CI {#heal-refusal}

Outside `--list`, `heal` in CI fails with a configuration error unless `ci.heal` is true. `heal --list` stays a discovery operation that writes nothing.

Healing buffers plan and grounding candidates privately. It writes them only after you answer the `ambercast heal` confirmation prompt, or after `--yes` answers it in advance. Replay attempts, including those under `--dry-run`, can still write contained evidence in the case directory under the runs directory.

Related: [ambercast heal](/ambercast/reference/cli/heal/#ci), [Healing model](/ambercast/explanation/healing-model/#confirmation-and-writes)

## The strongest problem sets the exit code {#exit-priority}

When results are mixed, the exit code is the strongest candidate. The priority is fixed at `2 > 3 > 4 > 1 > 5 > 0`. Iteration order and duplicate candidates do not change the result.

Related: [Exit codes](/ambercast/reference/exit-codes/#aggregation-priority), [Operating contract](/ambercast/agents/operating-contract/#next-action-by-exit-code), [Reading structured output](/ambercast/agents/reading-structured-output/#decision-tree)

---

# How ambercast compares
Source: https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/explanation/comparison/

Compare testing approaches by what each one keeps as the test asset, not by feature lists. ambercast keeps the prompt as the source and derives the plan from it. Code generation, record-and-replay, and direct-driving agents each keep something else.

## Code generation starts from recorded interaction {#code-generation-model}

In code generation, the test asset comes from captured interaction. Playwright documents codegen as recording browser actions and generating code to copy into an editor. The asset is then a script written for one runner.

ambercast puts an intermediate artifact in between. It normalizes the prompt, derives plan provenance, and builds a validated plan. The design favors assets that are not locked to a particular tool.

Related: [Philosophy](/ambercast/philosophy/), [Plan lifecycle and freshness](/ambercast/explanation/plan-lifecycle/)

## Record-and-replay keeps observed interaction {#record-and-replay-model}

Record-and-replay tools keep the actions performed in a browser session. Cypress documents Studio as recording real interactions and turning them into test commands. The recorded script becomes the asset inside the test suite.

ambercast keeps intent and element binding under separate contracts. The plan records `inputsDigest`, and grounding binds to `planDigest`. The derived plan and the grounding that locates elements can therefore change separately.

Related: [Replay and grounding](/ambercast/explanation/replay-and-grounding/), [Philosophy](/ambercast/philosophy/)

## Direct-driving agents act from the current session {#direct-driving-agent-model}

A direct-driving agent works inside a live browser session. It may act from screenshots and live tool calls, and it may leave no committed plan or grounding behind.

ambercast relies on reviewed, committed artifacts instead. A plan carries a producer-bundle fingerprint and schema-validated steps. Because ambercast builds and validates them before execution, you get artifacts you can read and inspect.

Related: [Using ambercast from an AI agent](/ambercast/agents/overview/), [Trust and security](/ambercast/explanation/trust-and-security/)

---

# Status and roadmap
Source: https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/explanation/status-and-roadmap/

The CLI has seven subcommands today: `init`, `generate`, `run`, `check`, `heal`, `view`, and `mcp`. `review` and baseline/restore are planned. Before 1.0, a change to a freshness input can require you to regenerate plans.

## Implemented in the current release {#implemented}

The CLI parser exposes `init`, `generate`, `run`, `check`, `heal`, `view`, and `mcp`. `ambercast mcp` serves six tools over stdio.

Chromium is the only supported browser.

Before 1.0, a minor release can include breaking changes. A change to a freshness input, such as the plan schema or the producer contract, forces you to regenerate existing plans. A report schema change alone only requires report consumers to update. In 0.2.0, for example, a producer-contract change made 0.1.0 plans stale. The [regeneration boundary](/ambercast/reference/compatibility/#regeneration-boundary) and the [0.2.0 changelog entry](/ambercast/reference/changelog/#release-020) show where regeneration is required.

Related: [CLI overview](/ambercast/reference/cli/overview/), [Compatibility](/ambercast/reference/compatibility/), [Changelog](/ambercast/reference/changelog/)

## Planned after the current boundary {#planned-after-current-boundary}

`review` and baseline/restore are planned. Firefox and WebKit support is planned, and so is a cloud version. MCP tools are already available.

Related: [ambercast review](/ambercast/reference/cli/review/), [MCP server](/ambercast/agents/mcp-server/)

## Version policy {#version-policy}

The [compatibility table](/ambercast/reference/compatibility/#compatibility-table) lists the published package versions. The product stays on 0.x until MVP.

Related: [Changelog](/ambercast/reference/changelog/), [Philosophy](/ambercast/philosophy/)

---

# Using ambercast from an AI agent
Source: https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/agents/overview/

This page tells an agent what to read before it starts and in what order to work. Agent pages own reading order, side effects, and action branching, Reference owns exact specifications, and How-to owns procedures.

## Read before acting {#read-before-acting}

The CLI has seven commands: `init`, `generate`, `run`, `check`, `heal`, `view`, and `mcp`. Before you change a test asset, read these four pages in order.

| Read | What you get |
| --- | --- |
| [Your first test in 5 minutes](/ambercast/tutorials/quick-start/) | The artifact loop and prerequisites |
| [Operating contract](/ambercast/agents/operating-contract/) | Side effects and approval boundaries |
| [CLI overview](/ambercast/reference/cli/overview/) | The exact contract of each command |
| [Reports](/ambercast/reference/reports/) | How to read the JSON report after a command |

Related: [Setup prompt](/ambercast/agents/setup-prompt/), [Reading structured output](/ambercast/agents/reading-structured-output/), [Machine-readable resources](/ambercast/agents/machine-readable-resources/)

## Work in a bounded loop {#bounded-loop}

The basic loop is to implement, write or adjust the requested `.test.md`, run it, and fix from the report. Take approval boundaries from the operating contract, not from a single result.

1. Implement the requested product change within the approved scope.
2. Write or adjust the requested `.test.md` so the prompt states the behavior to verify.
3. Run that `.test.md` and read its JSON report.
4. Fix from the report, then run again if needed.

`run` needs a trusted plan, so run `generate` on the requested `.test.md` first when none exists. `generate` writes the plan and grounding files beside the prompt.

Replay with complete grounding makes no AI call and needs no available provider. A grounding miss fails with exit 4 unless you pass `--resolve`.

Related: [Operating contract](/ambercast/agents/operating-contract/), [Reports](/ambercast/reference/reports/)

---

# Operating contract
Source: https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/agents/operating-contract/

The tables below say whether you may run a command and what to do after it. The CLI implements seven commands: `init`, `generate`, `run`, `check`, `heal`, `view`, and `mcp`.

## Command contract {#command-contract}

Check the precondition and the side effects before you run a command. `check` and `view` need no write storage, AI provider, or browser. `heal` holds plan and grounding changes until confirmation, but it can write attempt evidence under `runsDir` before approval and during `--dry-run`.

| Command | Precondition | Side effects | Needs approval? | Use in CI |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `init` | Write permission for the target directory. | May write the config, a sample prompt, a two-line `.gitignore` unit, and an `AGENTS.md` block. | Explicit user approval; `--yes` is not agent authorization. | Rejects non-interactive use without `--yes`. CI use does not change the approval boundary. |
| `generate` | A valid prompt and target. | Writes the plan and grounding unless `--list` or `--dry-run` is set; `--dry-run` writes nothing. After interactive consent, adds accepted secret names to `secrets.allow`. | Yes for consent and writes; show the diff before any commit. | Works once reviewed names are in `secrets.allow`. |
| `run` | A trusted plan for the selected prompt. | Persists the report; writes grounding only through the write-back gate. | Yes, unless the requested scope already allows writes. | Works, subject to the write-back policy. |
| `check` | An explicit test path, or a selection that discovery can find. | Reads prompts and artifacts only. | No. | Works. |
| `heal` | Every target the plan references sets `healReplayIsolation: "idempotent"` (the default is `stateful`). | May write attempt evidence; writes plan and grounding changes only after confirmation. | Explicit user approval; `--yes` is not agent authorization. | Refused unless `ci.heal` is `true`, except with `--list`. |
| `view` | stdin and stderr are terminals and `CI` is inactive, or you pass `--allow-headless`. Without `--port`, it tries up to 20 consecutive ports. | Starts a read-only HTTP server over persisted run reports; writes nothing. | No. | Needs `--allow-headless` when no terminal is attached. |
| `mcp` | The session-root directory exists. | Starts a stdio server; each tool follows its own write and approval boundaries. | Depends on the tool. | Depends on the tool. |

Outside `--list`, if a `heal` target is not idempotent, the command fails with `CONFIG_INVALID` and exit 2.

Related: [CLI overview](/ambercast/reference/cli/overview/), [ambercast init](/ambercast/reference/cli/init/#confirmation), [ambercast heal](/ambercast/reference/cli/heal/#preconditions), [ambercast run](/ambercast/reference/cli/run/#grounding-write-back)

## Prohibitions {#prohibitions}

These restrictions have no exceptions.

- Never place a literal secret value in a prompt, artifact, command, report, or message. Use a `SecretRef`, its environment variable, and the target's sink policy.
- `SECRET_LITERAL_REJECTED` comes from a narrow heuristic. It does not replace the prohibition above.
- Never add `@ambercast-secret` grant lines. For a name outside `secrets.allow`, get the operator's consent or ask them to add the reviewed name. `"*"` needs explicit approval because it accepts any name the AI proposes.
- In CI, do not run a real heal unless `ci.heal` is `true`.
- `--yes` answers the CLI confirmation prompt only. A dry run never commits.

Related: [Manage secrets](/ambercast/how-to/manage-secrets/), [Healing model](/ambercast/explanation/healing-model/#confirmation-and-writes)

## Next action by exit code {#next-action-by-exit-code}

When a command has several outcomes, the exit code follows a fixed priority, not the order of the results. Act on the code as follows.

| Exit | Meaning | Next safe action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | Success or no candidate | Inspect permitted diffs and continue within scope. |
| 1 | Command-specific negative result | Read the failed evidence. Do not heal or regenerate automatically. |
| 2 | Usage or configuration problem | Read `errors[].code` and fix that boundary. |
| 3 | Environment problem | Keep the JSON report and fix the environment, not the test. |
| 4 | Untrustworthy plan or grounding | For `MISSING_PLAN`, `STALE_PLAN`, and `INTEGRITY_VIOLATION`, use stale-artifact recovery. For `GROUNDING_UNRESOLVED`, rerun with `--resolve` only if the requested scope allows an AI call and a grounding write; otherwise report it. |
| 5 | Empty selection | Confirm the intended selection before you allow an empty set. |

Related: [Exit codes](/ambercast/reference/exit-codes/#aggregation-priority)

## Next action by report error {#next-action-by-report-error}

The report schema defines fifteen usage codes and eight environment codes. `INTERRUPTED` is run-scoped, and `skipped` rows mark the cases it affected. Each producible code belongs to exactly one row. The legacy `SECRET_GRANT_UNATTRIBUTABLE` is never produced and has no row.

| Codes | Next safe action |
| --- | --- |
| `CONFIG_INVALID`, `PROMPT_PATH_INVALID`, `TARGET_UNRESOLVED`, `EXECUTOR_UNSUPPORTED`, `PROMPT_AMBIGUOUS` | Read the named Reference page and fix the boundary without guessing values. |
| `SECRET_UNRESOLVED`, `SECRET_LITERAL_REJECTED`, `SECRET_ENV_VAR_COLLISION`, `SECRET_SYNTAX_REJECTED` | Fix the secret reference or environment variable. Never write the value into the prompt. |
| `SECRET_CONSENT_REQUIRED` | Get approval interactively or add reviewed names to `secrets.allow`. Do not retry as if consent were granted. |
| `MISSING_PLAN`, `STALE_PLAN`, `INTEGRITY_VIOLATION` | Treat the artifacts as untrusted and use stale-artifact recovery. |
| `GROUNDING_UNRESOLVED` | Rerun with `--resolve` only if the requested scope allows it; otherwise report it. If it still fails, read `details.reason` and report it instead of looping. |
| `BROWSER_LAUNCH_FAILED`, `AI_EXECUTOR_UNAVAILABLE`, `AI_RESPONSE_INVALID`, `FS_IO_ERROR`, `UNEXPECTED_CRASH` | Keep the JSON report and repair the environment. |
| `AGENTIC_STEP_FAILED`, `CASE_ABORTED` | Read `details`. Do not infer the case result; fix the environment or the call. |
| `INTERRUPTED` | Treat the remaining work as incomplete and infer no case result. |

Related: [Error codes](/ambercast/reference/error-codes/), [Reading structured output](/ambercast/agents/reading-structured-output/#decision-tree), [Troubleshoot common failures](/ambercast/how-to/troubleshoot/)

---

# Setup prompt
Source: https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/agents/setup-prompt/

Give the agent this prompt and it knows what to read, how far to go, and in what order to work. Paste it as written, in English.

## Copy-paste prompt {#copy-paste-prompt}

The prompt sets five rules.

1. The AI provider comes from an explicit override, then the configured provider. In `auto` mode, ambercast tries `claude` before `codex`.
2. `check` inspects artifacts without AI or a browser.
3. The default is to present a diff; commit only when asked.
4. The dev server belongs to the operator. The agent assumes the app already runs at the configured base URL and does not start, stop, or reconfigure it unless the operator explicitly asks.
5. With no file arguments, `generate`, `run`, and `heal` select every test that the configured discovery rules match.

~~~markdown
You are working on ambercast tests in this repository.
First read https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/tutorials/quick-start/. If the operator has not confirmed the application is running at the configured target base URL, ask for that confirmation before continuing. Then read https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/agents/operating-contract/, https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/agents/reading-structured-output/, and the relevant Reference page.
Work only on the requested .test.md prompt and its adjacent ambercast plan/grounding artifacts. Do not alter unrelated files.
Assume the project's dev server is already running at the configured target base URL. Do not start, stop, or reconfigure it unless explicitly asked.
Run check before treating existing artifacts as trustworthy. Use the documented provider configuration or invocation contract if an operation needs AI; fully grounded replay may not need a provider.
Treat generate, run, and heal as potentially side-effecting. Invoke `npx ambercast generate <requested.test.md>`, `npx ambercast run <requested.test.md>`, and `npx ambercast heal <requested.test.md>` only with the requested explicit `.test.md` path; use `npx ambercast check <requested.test.md>` with that same path. Before any unapproved artifact change, report the planned write scope. For heal, require explicit user approval; --yes only answers ambercast's confirmation prompt.
The no-argument forms of generate, run, and heal operate on all discovered tests that match the configured discovery rules. Use a no-argument form only when the operator explicitly requests that all-discovered-tests scope, and restate that scope before executing it.
Never place literal secret values in prompts, artifacts, commands, reports, or messages. Never write secret references or legacy `@ambercast-secret` grant lines in `.test.md` prompt text; a committed Plan or Grounding artifact may correctly contain a valid `secretRef` after local resolution and consent. When generate proposes a secret name outside `secrets.allow`, obtain the operator's approval interactively or ask them to add a reviewed name to `secrets.allow`; never use `"*"` without explicit operator approval. Never run a real heal in CI unless the user has explicitly authorized the required configuration and action.
When finished, present the complete diff and the command/report result. Do not commit unless explicitly asked.
~~~

Related: [Your first test in 5 minutes](/ambercast/tutorials/quick-start/), [Operating contract](/ambercast/agents/operating-contract/), [Environment variables](/ambercast/reference/environment-variables/)

---

# Reading structured output
Source: https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/agents/reading-structured-output/

A report belongs to the `generate`, `run`, `check`, `heal`, or `review` branch, selected by `command`. The sections below say where to start reading, when to stop, and when a result lets you continue.

## Decision tree {#decision-tree}

Read `command`, `reportPersistence`, `errors[].code`, and `results[].status` in that order. Only `run` has `reportPersistence`, with the values `persisted`, `failed`, and `not-attempted`. The schema defines a `review` branch, but the CLI has no `review` command.

If `errors[].code` holds any code, use the operating contract's report-error table before you change files. If it holds none, classify each `results[].status` by the rules for that command.

~~~
Read command.
├─ run: read reportPersistence first.
│  ├─ failed → keep the stdout report; treat persistence as an environment problem.
│  └─ persisted/not-attempted → continue to errors.
├─ generate/check/heal/review → continue to errors.
Read every errors[].code.
├─ any code → use the operating contract's report-error table before changing files.
└─ none → classify every results[].status for this command.
   ├─ listed/skipped → discovery-only or incomplete, not success.
   ├─ generate failed, run failed/error → read the evidence; do not heal or regenerate automatically.
   ├─ check other than fresh/fresh-without-grounding → artifacts are untrustworthy; use stale-artifact recovery.
   ├─ heal unresolved/partially-healed → report it; do not retry automatically.
   └─ any other status → continue only within approved scope.
~~~

Related: [Reports](/ambercast/reference/reports/), [Operating contract](/ambercast/agents/operating-contract/#next-action-by-report-error)

## Status means command-specific evidence {#status-by-command}

Each command has its own `results[].status` vocabulary. `listed` is discovery only, and `skipped` carries no execution evidence. Neither is success.

- `generate` uses `generated`, `would-generate`, `skipped-fresh`, `listed`, `failed`, and `skipped`.
- `run` uses `passed`, `failed`, `error`, `listed`, and `skipped`.
- `check` uses `fresh`, `stale`, `missing-plan`, `missing-grounding`, `stale-grounding`, `invalid-grounding`, `fresh-without-grounding`, `orphaned-plan`, `orphaned-grounding`, `invalid-artifact-name`, `listed`, and `skipped`.
- A completed `heal` row has `status: completed`, and `repairOutcome` is `healed`, `partially-healed`, `unresolved`, or `no-changes-needed`. `listed` and `skipped` rows carry identity only.

Related: [Generate results](/ambercast/reference/reports/#generate-results), [Run results](/ambercast/reference/reports/#run-results), [Check results](/ambercast/reference/reports/#check-results), [Heal results](/ambercast/reference/reports/#heal-results), [Plan lifecycle and freshness](/ambercast/explanation/plan-lifecycle/#grounding-binding)

## The exit code is a batch-level signal {#exit-code-signal}

Read the exit code only after the rows and errors, as a signal for the whole batch. Each report error also records its scope and kind in `errors[]`.

Related: [Exit codes](/ambercast/reference/exit-codes/#aggregation-priority), [Operating contract](/ambercast/agents/operating-contract/#next-action-by-exit-code)

---

# Official skill
Source: https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/agents/official-skill/

The skill teaches an agent the ambercast loop. This page explains how it differs from the setup prompt and the MCP server.

## What it is {#what-it-is}

ambercast ships an [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) skill at `skills/ambercast/SKILL.md`, named `ambercast`. It teaches a coding agent to write `<name>.test.md` prompts, drive `generate`, `run`, `check`, and `heal` through the CLI, read the `--json` report and the exit code, and choose the next safe action.

The [README](https://github.com/kotarotsubaki/ambercast#official-skill) covers the install methods: Claude Code, Codex CLI, `gh skill`-compatible agents, skills.sh, or a manual copy from the installed package.

## Intended role {#intended-role}

The skill teaches the loop. The [setup prompt](/ambercast/agents/setup-prompt/) sets the review-first boundary for one requested test. The [MCP server](/ambercast/agents/mcp-server/) is the connection for clients that call tools instead of a shell.

ambercast treats coding agents as first-class users next to the prompt and viewer surfaces for people.

Related: [Using ambercast from an AI agent](/ambercast/agents/overview/), [Setup prompt](/ambercast/agents/setup-prompt/), [MCP server](/ambercast/agents/mcp-server/), [Status and roadmap](/ambercast/explanation/status-and-roadmap/)

---

# MCP server
Source: https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/agents/mcp-server/

This page lists what you can call from an MCP client and where each call is documented. The server runs ambercast's browser E2E workflows: generate, run, check, and heal.

## Connection boundary {#connection-boundary}

`ambercast mcp` provides a portless stdio connection. One server process serves one session root. `--dir` selects it, and the process working directory is used when you omit it.

Files you pass to tools resolve against that root. `--sync-wait-ms` bounds the synchronous wait, and the default is 45000 ms.

The server exposes six tools: `ambercast_generate`, `ambercast_run`, `ambercast_check`, `ambercast_heal`, `ambercast_job_status`, and `ambercast_job_cancel`. The first four are the workflows, and the last two observe and cancel server-local jobs.

As [MCP Tools](/ambercast/reference/mcp-tools/#tool-table) explains, only `ambercast_generate` accepts `target`. The other workflow tools select targets from the plan.

Inputs, annotations, job records, `isError`, and the MCP error surface are on the same page. Register the process in your client as shown in [ambercast mcp](/ambercast/reference/cli/mcp/#client-registration).

## Changes from the planned design {#changes-from-the-planned-design}

| Earlier planned page | Implemented connection |
| --- | --- |
| Five planned tools, including `review` | Six tools, including job status and cancellation; `review` is not exposed |
| Report `outputSchema` published | `outputSchema` omitted |
| Heal preview only | Two-stage heal uses `applyToken` |
| Synchronous workflows only | Long `generate`, `run`, and heal-preview calls return jobs; status without an ID lists jobs |
| Server flags unspecified | `ambercast mcp` supports `--dir` and `--sync-wait-ms` |
| MCP errors unspecified | `HEAL_APPLY_TOKEN_INVALID`, `HEAL_APPLY_FAILED`, `JOB_NOT_FOUND`, and `JOB_FAILED` use a separate error surface |
| CLI inputs unspecified | Inputs exclude `headed`, `list`, `stale`, `json`, `yes`, and `configPath` |
| Exit code inferred from report | `_meta.exitCode` carries it explicitly |

Related: [MCP Tools](/ambercast/reference/mcp-tools/#tool-table), [ambercast mcp](/ambercast/reference/cli/mcp/#usage), [Reading structured output](/ambercast/agents/reading-structured-output/)
